Cluster-Robust Standard Errors for remix Models

sandwich_remix.Rd

Computes cluster-robust sandwich standard errors and confidence intervals for random-effects mixture models fitted using remix(). This allows for dependence between effect sizes belonging to the same cluster, such as multiple effect sizes from the same study.

Usage

sandwich_remix(model, cluster, type = c("CR1", "CR0"), rel_step = 1e-04)

Arguments

model

A fitted OpenMx model created using remix().

cluster

Vector identifying the cluster membership of each effect size, e.g., the study the effect size came from. Must have the same length and order as the observed effect sizes.

type

Cluster-robust covariance estimator. Either "CR1" (default), applying the correction G/(G-1), or "CR0", the unadjusted sandwich estimator, where G is the number of clusters (or, studies).

rel_step

Relative step size for numerical differentiation of the analytic score function. Defaults to 1e-4.

Value

An MxModel with attr("se_robust") containing the standard errors, and attr("sandwich") with vcov, the cluster-robust covariance matrix, vcov_free, the cluster-robust covariance matrix for the unique free model parameters, information, observed Fisher information matrix (negative Hessian of the log-likelihood), cluster_scores, the matrix of first derivatives of the log-likelihood for each cluster (rows) by free parameters (columns); n number of observed effect sizes, clusters number clusters G, npar, number of freely estimated parameters, type passed from input.

Details

Note that cluster-robust standard errors provide consistent inference for dependent effect sizes but do not affect the fitted parameter estimates, nor model the dependency in the data. CR0 and CR1 are large-sample approximations and may be unreliable when the number of clusters is small or mixture parameters are weakly identified.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(metamixture)

set.seed(1)

n <- 100
df <- metamixture::sim_remix_fixed_tau(n, es = 2)

res1 <- remix(
  yi = df$yi,
  vi = df$vi,
  classes = 2,
  tau2 = "equal"
)

# Original sample: one observation per cluster
sw1 <- sandwich_remix(
  res1,
  cluster = seq_len(n),
  type = "CR0"
)

# Duplicate observations exactly
df2 <- rbind(df, df)
df2$study <- rep(seq_len(n), 2)

res2 <- remix(
  yi = df2$yi,
  vi = df2$vi,
  classes = 2,
  tau2 = "equal"
)

sw2 <- sandwich_remix(
  res2,
  cluster = df2$study,
  type = "CR0"
)

# Compare robust covariance matrices
all.equal(
  attr(sw1, "sandwich")$vcov,
  attr(sw2, "sandwich")$vcov,
  tolerance = 1e-3
)
} # }
